body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}-\widehat M_{it})+\widehat B_2,\quad (\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\)

sampling_model.design: A deterministic common-start treatment block \(G\times W\) removes untreated potential outcomes from the completion sample; inference is conditional on the mask and the low-rank signal.
sampling_model.units: Conditional on the signal, row laws factor across units. Within each row the centered sub-Gaussian process has common stationary covariance and genuine finite-range block dependence with fixed known \(q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treated outcomes \(Y_{it}(1)\) are observed on \(G\times W\); their counterfactual mean component \(M_{it}\) is imputed from donor and pretreatment observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Donor and pretreatment factor Grams have explicit normalized eigenvalue bounds, and every target restriction retains at least the fixed fraction \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of the global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\). The proportional-cohort theorem has score variance of order \((nH)^{-1}\); the exponent-indexed frontier class has variance \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known rank is used in the native local nuclear-norm and rank-projection fits. Every target-specific native and auxiliary fit uses the same ordered \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\) chart and restriction map \(R_{it}\). A target-specific auxiliary fit measurable with respect to \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\) supports leave-neighborhood conditioning. Pretreatment residuals estimate finite-lag covariance, while fitted tangent weights and fitted projector Hessians estimate variance and serial curvature.
sampling_model.randomness: All probability statements are with respect to the rowwise error processes, conditional on \(M\), \(A\), and the realized treated potential outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Subgroup nuclear-norm completion permits inference for imputed entries under a large deterministic missing block and independent errors.
Leave-neighbor-out analysis gives weak-factor principal-component normality under dependent noise in a fully observed matrix.
Auxiliary leave-one-out estimators are asymptotically equivalent to the feasible nuclear-norm-based estimator without sample splitting.
Residual HAC estimators consistently estimate covariance matrices for weak-factor tensor loading scores with missing observations.
Convex and nonconvex matrix-completion solutions are tightly coupled under independent random entry sampling.
Double-debiased matrix completion yields confidence intervals for general linear forms under random entry sampling.
Residual block bootstrap confidence intervals cover fixed-cell treatment effects under weakly dependent factor errors.
Adjusted principal components provide pointwise factor and loading inference with general missing observations and dependent errors.
Factor and loading limit distributions are derived under general missing-data patterns.
Bias-aware confidence intervals attain uniformly correct coverage over weak interactive effects for admissible regressors.
Analytically bias-corrected alternating maximization is asymptotically normal for regression coefficients under unbalanced interactive effects.

body.tldr: A growing post window makes serial dependence enter deterministic-MNAR panel completion twice: through the long-run variance of the complete three-block tangent score and through a nonzero quadratic drift of rank projection. The kernel derives both objects for the implemented Choi--Yuan subgroup nuclear-norm estimator in target-indexed local charts, transfers a target-specific conditionally independent auxiliary fit through its masked proximal fixed point, estimates variance and drift from pretreatment residuals, and derives a uniform studentized limit under a global weak-signal envelope and fixed local-to-global signal comparability. A separate primitive class \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\) leaves the sharp signal--cohort--window frontier open with \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\) and no inherited remainder envelope.

project_justification.gap: Deterministic-MNAR panel completion has weak-signal inference only under independent errors and small one-date subgroups. Dependent-noise PCA, residual HAC for missing factors, and analytic bias correction for unbalanced interactive-effects regression do not control the implemented masked convex completion estimator at the shrinking standard-error scale of a growing causal window.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a native-optimizer second-order expansion whose first differential retains donor-window, treated-pre, and donor-pre overlap terms and whose projector curvature is contracted against finite-lag covariance.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a local-signal-indexed native expansion, a feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction defined in the same target chart as each auxiliary fit, an influence-weighted residual covariance estimator, a dependency-graph central limit theorem derived from conditional block dependence and factor-geometric score diffuseness, and uniform Wald coverage. A separate exponent-indexed class poses the sharp signal--cohort--window frontier without building a sufficient remainder envelope into its assumptions.

body.related_work: Choi and Yuan (2024) establish the same subgroup nuclear-norm and rank-projection architecture for deterministic-MNAR blocks; Theorem 2 strictly extends their one-date independent-noise limit, and Proposition 2 records the exact reduction. Choi and Yuan (2025) informs target-specific leave-neighbor conditioning for weak fully observed PCA; the present conditioning claim uses row-law factorization and genuine within-row block dependence and does not assert independence of a deleted neighborhood from its complement. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) informs the coupling of a proof-only leave-out fit to an implemented convex estimator. Chen et al. (2020) informs entrywise control of an actual convex matrix-completion solution under a different sampling design. Cen and Lam (2025) informs the residual-HAC feasible-oracle decomposition for missing weak-factor scores. Xia and Yuan (2021) informs the tangent-projection expansion for linear matrix functionals under random sampling. Xiong and Pelger (2023) and Su and Wang (2025) give pointwise or factor-score inference under general missing patterns, with different estimators and factor regimes. Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024) obtain fixed-cell bootstrap intervals rather than an analytic growing-window law. Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) obtain weak-factor-uniform bias-aware regression intervals but exclude the common-start subset policy regressor. Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) derive analytic missing-pattern bias corrections for alternating-maximization regression coefficients; that result does not cover a rank-projected completed-cell aggregate or its serial curvature. Ben-Michael and Feller (2026) motivate the aggregation last mile but do not state the native second-order theorem. A public theorem text for the 2026 Choi--Yuan rejoinder was not located, so it is not a load-bearing comparator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve identities and rank-one calculations are diagnostic evidence, not established results. The decisive unresolved step is uniform second-order transfer through the native masked optimizer, including centered quadratic aggregation, active-singular-space stability, penalty error, cubic terms, and feasible plug-in error at scale \(s\). Every perturbation bound must first be uniform in \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\); global-signal rates follow only after applying \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\). The score-diffuseness and dependency-graph lemmas must be derived from the stated factor geometry and conditional block dependence. If the rank-one Gaussian moving-average kill test leaves a nonvanishing interior term after correction, or if transfer requires \(\psi\asymp n\), the stated theorem must be withdrawn rather than weakened silently.
body.honest_scope: The proved-rate proposal class conditions on exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, conditionally independent rows, genuine within-row finite-range block dependence, a common stationary covariance, a fixed positive local-to-global signal comparability constant, a proportional treated cohort, bounded aspect ratios, and explicit donor/pre restricted-Gram bounds. It covers a realized cohort-window contrast with a growing but non-proportional-at-the-noise-boundary window. The separate frontier class varies \(g\asymp n^b\), \(H\asymp n^c\), and the global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\asymp n^a\), retains only \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\) and the other primitive geometric and moment conditions, uses \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\), and does not inherit the proved theorem's signal-window envelope or any negligible-remainder condition. Its window growth remains subject to \(W\subset J\), consecutiveness, and placement after \(S\). The project does not claim simultaneous event-time bands, unknown-rank validity, heterogeneous row covariance, hidden-block identification, rank overprojection robustness, or proportional-window inference when \(\psi\) is arbitrarily close to \(n^{1/2}\). The native transfer, feasible correction, coverage theorem, and sharp frontier are open; only their proof handles and falsification cases are specified.
